question: Should OpenClaw support native per-task model/provider hints in HEARTBEAT.md, or should scheduled model routing remain whole-turn and plugin/cron-owned?
rationale: Current main lacks the requested per-task heartbeat boundary, but adding it changes public task-file syntax, model precedence, and shared-session behavior; automation should not choose that product contract.

options.title: Fold into scheduled-job routing
options.body: Use the open cron/job-level model override track as the canonical way to run different scheduled work on different models, avoiding another heartbeat-specific routing syntax.

options.title: Add native HEARTBEAT.md task hints
options.body: Define task-level model/provider fields, group or split due tasks by effective model, and cover precedence, validation, timestamps, and session restoration in docs and tests.

options.title: Keep whole-turn plugin routing only
options.body: Document that before_model_resolve can route an entire heartbeat turn and close the exact per-task split unless a missing generic plugin seam is approved.

recommendation.title: Fold into scheduled-job routing
recommendation.body: Use the open cron/job-level model override track as the canonical way to run different scheduled work on different models, avoiding another heartbeat-specific routing syntax.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily product scope between core syntax, plugin routing, and ClawHub/community ownership, and steipete has made the closest related routing-scope decisions.
